123|### Cause 2 — Completion report rejected with HTTP 413 (payload > Fastify 1 MiB default)
124|
125|**Summary.** After a fully successful agent run + `commitAndPush`
126|(commit AND push succeed), the runner's `complete-execution` POST exceeds the
127|backend JSON body limit and is rejected with 413. The daemon's generic catch
128|(`runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`, deployed 0.1.0 without reason attachment) reports
129|a bare interrupt and rethrows → `exit(1)` → systemd restart → re-claim → the
130|agent re-runs for minutes → commit+push again → 413 again. Deterministic loop;
131|each lap is recorded as one interruption + auto-resume and burns a full stage
132|run. The 413 trigger on the observed task is `collectTaskFiles`
133|(`runner/daemon.js:1820` / deployed `daemon.js:1346`): top-level task-doc files
134|up to ~1 MiB total — and this task's folder holds 2.8 MiB including many
135|top-level PNG screenshots each under the 256 KiB per-file cap — plus the 20 KiB
136|output and JSON envelope, against Fastify's default 1 MiB limit
137|(`api/index.js:116` sets no `bodyLimit`; the only explicit `bodyLimit` in the
138|API is the accessibility route).
139|
140|**Pros (for).**
141|- Smoking gun in the server2-alpha journal (`journalctl --user
142|  -u kainbain-runner-server2-alpha`): on 11-20, five consecutive cycles of
143|  `Committed <sha> (pushed: true)` → `Runner failed: Backend 413 on
144|  /tasks/7f6220c3-.../complete-execution` → `Main process exited, status=1`
145|  → `Scheduled restart job, restart counter 830→834`, at 21:19, 21:29, 21:35,
146|  21:43, 21:47 — exactly matching the five `finished` → bare-interrupt pairs
147|  in task `7f6220c3` history.
148|- Worktree forensics agree: `kb-7f6220c3` holds the pushed stage-output commits
149|  with matching timestamps, and `origin` has them — proving failure happened
150|  strictly after push.
151|- Deterministic: same task files every lap → same 413 → loop only ends via the
152|  death-bound park (observed: parked at count 7).
153|- Explains why the newest, longest, most asset-heavy stages (Merge resolver
154|  with proof screenshots) interrupt while short stages complete.
155|
156|**Cons (against).**
157|- Proven for exactly one task-stage so far (`7f6220c3` Merge resolver, 5
158|  interrupts); the other 10 post-`finished` bare interrupts are unexamined.
159|- Cannot explain the 99 sub-15s interrupts (413 only happens at completion,
160|  minutes in).
161|- Backend 413 leaves no task-history trace of its own (the backend rejects
162|  before routing), so backend history alone can never confirm/deny further
163|  cases — runner journals are required.
164|
165|**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
166|- `7f6220c3` (screenshot task; Merge-resolver window 11-20 21:15–21:47):
167|  backend access/error log for the five 413s (confirm size vs limit);
168|  preserve `kb-7f6220c3` worktree (do not reap) — 2.8 MiB task-docs exhibit.
169|- Journal sweep on both runner hosts for `Backend 413` across all tasks/dates
170|  (server2-alpha: 5 hits since 11-19, all this task; local-alpha journal still
171|  needed — host `192.168.1.206`, user `server`).
172|- Any other task whose `finished` → interrupt gap is seconds with a preceding
173|  multi-minute run is a 413 suspect; check runner journals first, backend
174|  history second (it will be bare).

229|interrupt (bare on 0.1.0) and the restart cycle begins. server2-alpha is a
230|remote runner over LAN, so it is exposed to every network blip and every

352|## 4. Amplifier (not a root cause): re-queue + display mechanics multiply every flake
353|
354|These do not initiate interrupts, but they turn each one into the screenshot's
355|"quite common" impression and into parked tasks:
356|
357|- **Instant priority re-dispatch, no backoff.** Every interrupt flips to
358|  `in_stage` with Rule-0 priority and dispatches in ~150ms
359|  (`performStartupRecovery`, `scheduleTick.js:178-181`, `findResumedCandidate`),
360|  so the same failing runner re-claims immediately — tight loops (18s laps on
361|  `c5c465c4`) instead of spaced retries, and no window for the sibling runner
362|  or the operator to intervene.
363|- **Death counter counts capacity refusals as deaths.** `interruptExecution`
364|  increments `runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally — including graceful
365|  `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` refusals where nothing died. Five cap refusals on one
366|  stage = `runner-death-loop` park (`isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`),
367|  mislabelling a full disk-table as dying runners (42 escalations fleet-wide;
368|  `c5c465c4` hit 27).
369|- **`Tried N times` counts resumes as tries.** `summarizeStageRuns`
370|  (`frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js:483-536`) sets `tryCount`
371|  to the number of grouped timeline rows per stage — `Advanced` + `Moved` +
372|  `Failed` + every `Resumed` row (each auto-resume writes one, `autoResumeTask`
373|  `:71-78`). Genuine failback cycles (e.g. four `CI command failed with exit
374|  code 1` round-trips on `7f6220c3`) and interrupt/resume cycles are summed
375|  into one scary number.
376|- **`Auto-resumed after server restart` mislabels runner interrupts.**
377|  `autoResumeTask` uses one history string for both recovery routes, so 100
378|  runner-path resumes display as server restarts that never happened (0
379|  recorded) — directly feeding the "server flake" reading of the report.

1|# WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS — high level of task interruptions
2|
3|Task: `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4` ("noticing a high level of interruptions").
4|Date: 2026-11-21. Stage: DO research (investigatory only — no solutions proposed).
5|
6|## 0. Inputs
7|
8|- **Bug report**: many tasks end with interruptions suggesting flakiness; reporter
9|  notes a `local-alpha` runner restart-loop incident and wonders if it is related;
10|  interruptions "should happen rarely but they are seemingly quite common".
11|- **Screenshot** (`assets/image.png`): task `7f6220c3` ("add support for projects
12|  having the kainbain docs in a seperate repo") showing repeated
13|  "Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue" rows and high
14|  "Tried N times" counts (Merge resolver ×6, Quick review ×6, Automated
15|  tests ×10, In Progress ×11).
16|- **Survey result**: the Questionnaire stage recorded `Survey completed (none)` —
17|  the `question-me` skill requested no survey questions, so there is no
18|  `SURVEY.md` with human answers. All evidence below comes from repo code,
19|  the live backend API, runner worktrees, and the runner systemd journal.
20|
21|## 1. How interruptions work (mechanics primer)
22|
23|Two code paths flip a task to `interrupted` (verified by repo search):
24|
25|1. **Server-restart path** — `reconcileInterruptedRuns`
26|   (`api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js`): at boot, any task left in
27|   `running_agent` / `running_ci` / `running_merge` / `advancing` (see
28|   `ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES` in `api/flow/scheduler/orphanedRunningStatuses.js`)
29|   with no engine owner becomes `interrupted`, history
30|   `Stage execution interrupted by server restart`.
31|2. **Runner path** — `POST /tasks/:id/interrupt` (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js:1067`)
32|   → `executionLedger.interruptExecution` (`api/flow/executionLedger.js:608`):
33|   the runner drops its lease and the task re-queues as `interrupted`, history
34|   `Runner <id> interrupted execution <exec> — lease dropped, re-queues as
35|   interrupted[ — Reason: <reason>]`. This is the ONLY writer of that history
36|   string, and the route requires runner auth, so every such entry was sent by
37|   an authenticated runner daemon.
38|
39|Recovery: `autoResumeTask` (`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js`) flips
40|`interrupted` → `in_stage` with Rule-0 queue priority and history
41|`Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue` — **including when no
42|server restart happened** (runner-path interrupts resume through the same
43|function via `scheduleTick`, pickup ≈150ms per `performStartupRecovery` docs in
44|`api/flow/startupRecovery.js`). Anti-loop guard: consecutive interrupts on the
45|same task+stage increment `runnerInterruptCount`; at `MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS = 5`
46|(`api/flow/executionLedger.js:17`) the task is parked for the operator
47|(`runner-death-loop` in `api/flow/scheduler/isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`).
48|
49|## 2. Fleet-wide numbers (live backend, project `0fd41821`, 61 tasks, 2026-11-21)
50|
51|| Signal | Count | Notes |
52||---|---|---|
53|| Runner-path interrupts (`interrupted execution`) | 118 | across 30/61 tasks (~half the project) |
54|| Server-restart interrupts (`interrupted by server restart`) | **0** | no task, ever in retained history |
55|| `Execution recovered after server restart` | **0** | same |
56|| `Auto-resumed after server restart` entries | 100 | label fires for runner interrupts too |
57|| Runner split | local-alpha 96 / server2-alpha 22 | local-alpha dominates 4:1 |
58|| With `Reason:` suffix | 49 | **all 49 are the same reason** (Cause 1) |
59|| Bare (no reason) | 69 | cause invisible from backend history |
60|| Interrupt ≤15s after `started` (median 4.7s) | 99 | dies before/without `prompted`, i.e. in worktree setup |
61|| Interrupt ≥2min after `started` | 15 | post-harness: commit/push/complete phase |
62|| Death-streak escalations (`Runner deaths escalated`) | 42 | tasks parked at count ≥ 5 |
63|
64|Timing detail: between the runner's `started` and `prompted` progress events
65|(`runner/daemon.js:1975` → `:2061`) the only uncaught fallible step is
66|`prepareWorkdir` (`runner/daemon.js:1984`; doc-sync and prompt-report are
67|try/caught). So a `started` → interrupt gap of seconds with no `prompted` event
68|localises the fault to worktree preparation (or the process dying there).
69|Between `finished` (`runner/daemon.js:2213`) and completion sit `commitAndPush`,
70|`sendLogs`, verdict, `collectTaskFiles`, and `client.complete`.
71|
72|Deployed runner vintage: live runners report `0.1.0`, built from main
73|`f430f53` (2026-11-11); repo is at `0.2.0`. The deployed build HAS the 10-29
74|worktree-cap graceful path (`25feee39`) but LACKS the 11-21 interrupt-reason
75|and deterministic-git-failure handling (`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in
76|`7ac148ce`). Runner rollout is backend-nudged, at most daily per runner, idle
77|converge (`docs/runner-update-runbook.md`), so rollout lag is expected.
78|
79|## 3. Possible causes
80|
81|### Cause 1 — Worktree-capacity exhaustion loop (`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, cap ~5)
82|
83|**Summary.** The runner refuses new work when its work-root holds ~5 live/orphan
84|workdirs and none are stale enough to evict; it reports an interrupt with a
85|reason and keeps polling (`runner/daemon.js:2299-2314`). The task re-queues with
86|Rule-0 priority and is immediately re-claimed — often by the same still-full
87|runner — producing a tight interrupt/resume cycle. Each refusal also increments
88|the runner-death counter, so a capacity problem eventually parks the task as a
89|suspected death loop.
90|
91|**Pros (for).**
92|- Direct textual evidence: all 49 reasoned interrupts (41% of the fleet total)
93|  carry `Reason: Runner workdir unavailable: Worktree cap reached (~5); ...
94|  (every orphan was used recently, nothing stale to evict)`. Both hosts appear
95|  (`/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain` = local-alpha host, `/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain` =
96|  server2-alpha host).
97|- Timing fits: cap refusal happens inside `prepareWorkdir`, seconds after
98|  `started` — matching the dominant ≤15s bucket.
99|- Code path returns (no crash) and keeps polling, which explains rapid
100|  re-claim cycles without process restarts.
101|- Crash loops (Causes 2–4) leave orphan workdirs behind (observed: 5 orphans
102|  listed at every server2-alpha boot on 11-20), so this cause is also a
103|  second-order effect of the other causes — they feed each other.
104|
105|**Cons (against).**
106|- Explains at most 49/118 interrupts; the 69 bare interrupts cannot be cap
107|  refusals on the deployed builds (both runners demonstrably emit the cap
108|  reason since the 10-29/11-11 build, and reasoned cap interrupts appear on
109|  both hosts).
110|- Does not explain the ≥2min post-`finished` interrupts (15 cases).
111|- Reasoned cap interrupts cluster 11-09 → 11-17; the 11-19/11-20 spike
112|  (48 bare) needs a different driver.
113|
114|**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
115|- `350ca162` (12 cap interrupts), `db24c124` (9), `7b69d365` (6), `3c12ffcd`
116|  (5), `f56e9878` (4), `1f8959ca` (5) — confirm each shows the cap reason and
117|  same-runner re-claim.
118|- Runner-side: work-root occupancy time series per host around 11-09 and
119|  11-16/17; orphan-staleness / LRU-eviction decisions in daemon logs.
120|- Backend: `GET /tasks/<id>` history for `WORKTREE_CAP` reason strings is the
121|  cheapest ongoing detector (no host access needed).
122|
123|### Cause 2 — Completion report rejected with HTTP 413 (payload > Fastify 1 MiB default)
124|
125|**Summary.** After a fully successful agent run + `commitAndPush`
126|(commit AND push succeed), the runner's `complete-execution` POST exceeds the
127|backend JSON body limit and is rejected with 413. The daemon's generic catch
128|(`runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`, deployed 0.1.0 without reason attachment) reports
129|a bare interrupt and rethrows → `exit(1)` → systemd restart → re-claim → the
130|agent re-runs for minutes → commit+push again → 413 again. Deterministic loop;
131|each lap is recorded as one interruption + auto-resume and burns a full stage
132|run. The 413 trigger on the observed task is `collectTaskFiles`
133|(`runner/daemon.js:1820` / deployed `daemon.js:1346`): top-level task-doc files
134|up to ~1 MiB total — and this task's folder holds 2.8 MiB including many
135|top-level PNG screenshots each under the 256 KiB per-file cap — plus the 20 KiB
136|output and JSON envelope, against Fastify's default 1 MiB limit
137|(`api/index.js:116` sets no `bodyLimit`; the only explicit `bodyLimit` in the
138|API is the accessibility route).
139|
140|**Pros (for).**
141|- Smoking gun in the server2-alpha journal (`journalctl --user
142|  -u kainbain-runner-server2-alpha`): on 11-20, five consecutive cycles of
143|  `Committed <sha> (pushed: true)` → `Runner failed: Backend 413 on
144|  /tasks/7f6220c3-.../complete-execution` → `Main process exited, status=1`
145|  → `Scheduled restart job, restart counter 830→834`, at 21:19, 21:29, 21:35,
146|  21:43, 21:47 — exactly matching the five `finished` → bare-interrupt pairs
147|  in task `7f6220c3` history.
148|- Worktree forensics agree: `kb-7f6220c3` holds the pushed stage-output commits
149|  with matching timestamps, and `origin` has them — proving failure happened
150|  strictly after push.
151|- Deterministic: same task files every lap → same 413 → loop only ends via the
152|  death-bound park (observed: parked at count 7).
153|- Explains why the newest, longest, most asset-heavy stages (Merge resolver
154|  with proof screenshots) interrupt while short stages complete.
155|
156|**Cons (against).**
157|- Proven for exactly one task-stage so far (`7f6220c3` Merge resolver, 5
158|  interrupts); the other 10 post-`finished` bare interrupts are unexamined.
159|- Cannot explain the 99 sub-15s interrupts (413 only happens at completion,
160|  minutes in).
161|- Backend 413 leaves no task-history trace of its own (the backend rejects
162|  before routing), so backend history alone can never confirm/deny further
163|  cases — runner journals are required.
164|
165|**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
166|- `7f6220c3` (screenshot task; Merge-resolver window 11-20 21:15–21:47):
167|  backend access/error log for the five 413s (confirm size vs limit);
168|  preserve `kb-7f6220c3` worktree (do not reap) — 2.8 MiB task-docs exhibit.
169|- Journal sweep on both runner hosts for `Backend 413` across all tasks/dates
170|  (server2-alpha: 5 hits since 11-19, all this task; local-alpha journal still
171|  needed — host `192.168.1.206`, user `server`).
172|- Any other task whose `finished` → interrupt gap is seconds with a preceding
173|  multi-minute run is a 413 suspect; check runner journals first, backend
174|  history second (it will be bare).
175|
176|### Cause 3 — local-alpha premature-death loop in worktree setup (bare, ~5s, no `prompted`)
177|
178|**Summary.** The volume-dominant signature: `local-alpha` claims a task
179|(`started`), then ~5–11s later reports a bare interrupt without ever emitting
180|`prompted` — i.e. it dies inside `prepareWorkdir` (git fetch/worktree-add,
181|residue handling, LRU eviction, docs worktree) or the process dies there — then
182|re-claims ~20–60s later and repeats until the death bound parks the task. This
183|matches the reporter's "local-alpha restart loop" incident. The underlying fault
184|is unknown precisely because the deployed 0.1.0 build attaches no reason on the
185|generic path (reason support landed 11-21 in `046a6391`, after these events).
186|
187|**Pros (for).**
188|- Dominant by volume: 96/118 interrupts are local-alpha; 99/118 fleet-wide fall
189|  in the ≤15s bucket (median 4.7s); the bare-by-day spike is 11-19 (30) and
190|  11-20 (18).
191|- Two textbook exhibits: `c5c465c4` — 28 bare local-alpha interrupts ~18s apart
192|  on 11-19 12:15–12:37; `7f6220c3` — In-Progress loop (11-20 15:38–15:43, ×5 to
193|  escalation), Quick-review loop (18:39–18:41, ×4), plus 10:16 and 13:34
194|  single-shot deaths on 11-21 seconds after a manual resume.
195|- Localisation is tight: no `prompted` ⇒ pre-harness ⇒ `prepareWorkdir` region
196|  (only uncaught fallible step there).
197|- The deployed build cannot exonerate or name the fault (no reason), so "bare +
198|  fast + local" is exactly what any setup-phase fault looks like on 0.1.0.
199|
200|**Cons (against).**
201|- Root fault genuinely unidentified — could be git (lock/fetch/push-race),
202|  disk, permissions, docs-worktree handling (note: `7f6220c3` IS the
203|  separate-docs-repo task, and stage output mentions docs worktrees), a stale
204|  mirror, or backend-call failures during setup. No evidence yet discriminates.
205|- Cycle period varies (~18s on `c5c465c4` vs ~40–60s on `7f6220c3`), suggesting
206|  possibly two sub-mechanisms (in-process re-claim vs systemd restart); local
207|  restart counters are unknown from here.
208|- "Restart loop" implies process restarts, but a tight claim→interrupt→re-claim
209|  cycle without restarts would look identical in backend history.
210|
211|**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
212|- `c5c465c4` (28×, 11-19 12:15–12:37), `7f6220c3` (In Progress 11-20
213|  15:38–15:43; Quick review 18:39–18:41; 11-21 10:16 + 13:34), `350ca162`
214|  (12× local) — need the **local-alpha daemon journal on the backend host**
215|  (`192.168.1.206`, `~server`, systemd user unit) for those windows: the
216|  `Runner failed: <message>` line names the fault, and restart-counter lines
217|  separate crash-loops from re-claim loops.
218|- local-alpha build provenance: confirm it is also pre-11-21 (expected bare);
219|  after the 0.2.x rollout, bare interrupts should vanish and reasons should
220|  name this cause directly — re-run the §2 counts as the before/after test.
221|- Work-root/disk/git-mirror health on the backend host at those times.
222|
223|### Cause 4 — Backend-unreachable / 502 windows crashing the daemon mid-run
224|
225|**Summary.** The runner daemon treats backend call failures as fatal: `fetch
226|failed` (undici network error) and `Backend 502` crash the process (`exit(1)` →
227|systemd restart). When the failure lands inside an assignment (claim, logs,
228|progress, complete, heartbeat/renewal handling), the generic catch reports an
229|interrupt (bare on 0.1.0) and the restart cycle begins. server2-alpha is a
230|remote runner over LAN, so it is exposed to every network blip and every
231|backend restart/502 window.
232|
233|**Pros (for).**
234|- server2-alpha journal since 11-19: 501 × `fetch failed` and 16 × `Backend
235|  502` (`/runners/heartbeat`, `/runners/dispatch`); the idle-loop sample
236|  (11-19 11:15:20–11:15:44) shows three consecutive `fetch failed` crashes with
237|  restart counters 366→367 — proving the daemon exits rather than retries.
238|- A proven backend 502 window on 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 (seven heartbeat 502s,
239|  new pid each ~6s) coincides with backend build 637 `deployedAt`
240|  2026-11-20T20:40:14Z and `engine.updatedAt` 20:40:57Z — i.e. a real backend
241|  restart/downtime window, observed from the runner side.
242|- Any in-flight assignment spanning such a window (or a LAN blip) on the 0.1.0
243|  build becomes a bare interrupt — consistent with scattered bare interrupts on
244|  both runners.
245|
246|**Cons (against).**
247|- The 11-20 20:40 backend restart demonstrably did NOT interrupt the in-flight
248|  Quick-review stage on `7f6220c3` (it completed 20:44:48), so heartbeat/502
249|  windows are survivable mid-run at least sometimes — the fatality depends on
250|  which call fails (fatal inside `executeAssignment`'s try, tolerated in the
251|  renewal/heartbeat path).
252|- No bare interrupt has yet been timestamp-matched to a specific 502/fetch-fail
253|  crash mid-assignment; the 501 `fetch failed` lines are dominated by idle-loop
254|  polls with no task impact.
255|- local-alpha (96/118 interrupts) likely talks to the backend over localhost,
256|  where network blips are far less plausible — this cause fits server2-alpha
257|  better than the dominant offender.
258|
259|**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
260|- Timestamp-join: server2-alpha `Runner failed: fetch failed` / `Backend 502`
261|  lines against `started` → interrupt pairs on server2-alpha tasks (`db24c124`,
262|  `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`) — a mid-assignment crash
263|  proves this cause per case.
264|- Backend availability log (or reverse-proxy log — the 502 implies a proxy or
265|  gateway in front) for 11-19 → 11-21 to enumerate real downtime windows.
266|- Renewal/heartbeat failure semantics: confirm from code + logs that mid-run
267|  heartbeat loss is tolerated (lease TTL) while in-`try` call failures are
268|  fatal — the boundary determines how often this cause bites.
269|
270|### Cause 5 — Stage-end commit/push failure crash loop (pre-commit hooks, git faults)
271|
272|**Summary.** A stage-end `commitAndPush` failure on the 0.1.0 build takes the
273|generic interrupt+rethrow path: bare interrupt, `exit(1)`, systemd restart,
274|re-claim, re-run, same failure — the classic crash loop. Deterministic faults
275|(pre-commit hook rejecting files, e.g. corrupt PNGs) loop forever until the
276|death bound parks the task. This is the documented "10,000 restarts" incident
277|class.
278|
279|**Pros (for).**
280|- Documented precedent: task `1cae113f` survey (Round 1, Q2) states "the runner
281|  restarted over 10,000 times in a crash loop after the commit failed", with
282|  corrupt images vs the pre-commit hook as the trigger (Q6); the fix
283|  (deterministic-failure → failed completion, no crash; `046a6391`) merged
284|  11-21 09:38 — after every observed interruption — and still needs runner
285|  rollout.
286|- Code path exists and is fatal on the deployed build (generic catch at
287|  `runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`; the 0.1.0 build predates the
288|  `isDeterministicGitFailure` branch).
289|- Comment trail in code already links rethrow-on-git-fault to "crash-loops
290|  under Restart=always" (`runner/daemon.js:2322-2324`) and restart storms to
291|  task death loops (`runner/daemon.js:2301-2303`, ref `e79b1d25`).
292|- `db49d6c6` ("Fix runner recovery commits failing on pre-commit hooks") shows
293|  hook/commit friction is a live, recurring theme, not a one-off.
294|
295|**Cons (against).**
296|- On the forensically examined case (`7f6220c3` Merge resolver), commit+push
297|  SUCCEEDED in all five cycles (journal `Committed … (pushed: true)` + origin
298|  has the SHAs) — this cause is affirmatively ruled out there; the killer was
299|  the 413 (Cause 2).
300|- No other `finished` → interrupt case has yet been shown to lack a
301|  stage-output commit; worktree forensics (`kb-<taskId>` dirs, still present
302|  for `158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`) can confirm/deny per case
303|  but has not been run beyond `7f6220c3`.
304|- Sub-15s interrupts cannot be commit failures (commit happens minutes in, post
305|  `finished`).
306|
307|**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
308|- `1cae113f` (incident record + fix), `db49d6c6` (recovery-commit hook
309|  failures), `e79b1d25` (referenced death-loop task) — prior art and fix
310|  status.
311|- For each remaining post-`finished` bare interrupt: does `kb-<taskId>`
312|  contain a stage-output commit for that execution (→ Cause 2/4 territory) or
313|  not (→ this cause)? Plus the daemon journal `Runner failed:` line.
314|- Post-rollout check: deterministic commit failures should surface as FAILED
315|  completions with `gitFailure` payloads (per `1cae113f`), never as interrupts.
316|
317|### Cause 6 — Backend server restarts (incl. self-deploys) orphaning running tasks
318|
319|**Summary.** The reporter's alternate hypothesis, and what the UI label
320|("Auto-resumed after server restart") literally claims: backend restarts
321|(`deploy.sh` `restart_service`, crashes, OOM, operator restarts) orphan
322|`running_*` tasks, which reconcile to `interrupted` at boot.
323|
324|**Pros (for).**
325|- Mechanically real: `deploy.sh` full deploys call `restart_service`
326|  (`systemctl --user restart kainbain.service`); the reconcile path exists and
327|  is tested (`api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js`).
328|- A real backend restart/downtime window was observed 11-20 20:40:14–20:40:57
329|  (build 637 `deployedAt`, engine `updatedAt`, runner-visible 502s).
330|- The UI labels every auto-resume "after server restart", priming this reading.
331|
332|**Cons (against — strong).**
333|- **Zero occurrences in retained history across all 61 tasks**: no `Stage
334|  execution interrupted by server restart`, no `Execution recovered after
335|  server restart`. All 118 interrupts are runner-initiated lease drops.
336|- The five most recent deploys (11-19 → 11-21, spanning the interruption spike)
337|  are all `--publish-only` (`registry + dist`), which `exit 0` before
338|  `restart_service` (`deploy.sh:1699-1712`, "prod untouched") — no restarts.
339|- The one observed restart (11-20 20:40) demonstrably orphaned nothing: the
340|  in-flight stage completed normally at 20:44:48.
341|- 1193 deploys in history with a 0-observed orphan rate suggests restarts
342|  either land on idle engines or claims survive them; either way this is not
343|  the current driver.
344|
345|**Tasks / evidence wanted (to keep this ruled out, cheaply).**
346|- Backend uptime/restarts: backend host journal for the API unit + `build.json`
347|  `deployedAt` vs `GET /status/observability` `engine.updatedAt` divergence as
348|  a restart detector.
349|- Ongoing: any future `interrupted by server restart` history line re-opens
350|  this cause immediately (grep task histories; currently zero).
351|
352|## 4. Amplifier (not a root cause): re-queue + display mechanics multiply every flake
353|
354|These do not initiate interrupts, but they turn each one into the screenshot's
355|"quite common" impression and into parked tasks:
356|
357|- **Instant priority re-dispatch, no backoff.** Every interrupt flips to
358|  `in_stage` with Rule-0 priority and dispatches in ~150ms
359|  (`performStartupRecovery`, `scheduleTick.js:178-181`, `findResumedCandidate`),
360|  so the same failing runner re-claims immediately — tight loops (18s laps on
361|  `c5c465c4`) instead of spaced retries, and no window for the sibling runner
362|  or the operator to intervene.
363|- **Death counter counts capacity refusals as deaths.** `interruptExecution`
364|  increments `runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally — including graceful
365|  `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` refusals where nothing died. Five cap refusals on one
366|  stage = `runner-death-loop` park (`isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`),
367|  mislabelling a full disk-table as dying runners (42 escalations fleet-wide;
368|  `c5c465c4` hit 27).
369|- **`Tried N times` counts resumes as tries.** `summarizeStageRuns`
370|  (`frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js:483-536`) sets `tryCount`
371|  to the number of grouped timeline rows per stage — `Advanced` + `Moved` +
372|  `Failed` + every `Resumed` row (each auto-resume writes one, `autoResumeTask`
373|  `:71-78`). Genuine failback cycles (e.g. four `CI command failed with exit
374|  code 1` round-trips on `7f6220c3`) and interrupt/resume cycles are summed
375|  into one scary number.
376|- **`Auto-resumed after server restart` mislabels runner interrupts.**
377|  `autoResumeTask` uses one history string for both recovery routes, so 100
378|  runner-path resumes display as server restarts that never happened (0
379|  recorded) — directly feeding the "server flake" reading of the report.
380|

1|# Runner update runbook
2|
3|Operator procedures for the runner self-update channel (Option A,
4|`docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md`): cutting releases,
5|rolling back, migrating hosts to the wrapper, and triaging a runner
6|that says out of date. The backend directs version selection but never
7|serves runner bytes (R05) — every procedure below preserves that.
8|
9|## Cutting a runner release (normal path)
10|
11|The tag is the version source of truth; the pipeline cuts it.
12|
13|1. Bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json` (plain semver for
14|   fleet releases, e.g. `0.2.0`; suffixed tags like `0.3.0-rc.1` for
15|   canaries — v1 runners skip pre-releases automatically).
16|2. If the release needs a newer backend API, update the
17|   `requires.backendApi` range in the same file (e.g.
18|   `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`). The release builder refuses manifests without a
19|   compat claim, and runners filter on this range.
20|3. Merge to the main line through the normal review flow.
21|4. Publish the runner (`publish.sh` with the runner component). The
22|   publish cuts and pushes the annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which
23|   triggers `runner-release.yml`: full update-channel test gate, four
24|   platform archives, signed `manifest.json` + `.minisig`, GitHub
25|   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
26|   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).
27|5. Raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the new version on
28|   the backend. That is the one managed place: trailers light the
29|   "update available" badge and the backend auto-nudges command-capable
30|   ones (`requestUpdate`, at most daily per runner). Runners converge
31|   on idle with no SSH. Leave `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` alone
32|   unless this is a breaking release (the 409 floor stops dispatch).
33|
34|## Cutting a runner release (emergency path)
35|
36|When the pipeline cannot cut the tag (CI down, urgent patch), tag by
37|hand from the release commit — the same builder runs:
38|
39|```
40|git tag -a runner-vX.Y.Z -m "Runner runner-vX.Y.Z" <full-sha>
41|git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z
42|```
43|
44|Then follow step 5 above. Never move an existing tag: cut a patch
45|version forward instead.
46|
47|## Rollback drill (bad release, no host access needed)
48|
49|1. Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release so `releases/latest`
50|   resolves to the prior tag.
51|2. Lower `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (and
52|   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` if it was raised past the bad
53|   version) to stop badge nagging and 409 loops.
54|3. Cut a patch release forward (normal path above). The updater never
55|   downgrades: runners still on older versions pick the prior release
56|   up on their next idle check, while runners already on the bad
57|   release stay there until the patch supersedes it.
58|4. Two automatic outs: a release that crashes on boot rolls itself
59|   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
60|   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
61|   is cut.
62|
63|Drill timing to record: un-publish → badges clear, patch cut →
64|fleet converged.
65|
66|## Migrating a host to the wrapper
67|
68|Direct `node main.js` units re-exec the same old directory on every
69|restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
70|versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at
71|the stable wrapper shim — onto the SAME version (no update is staged,
72|so the fleet version does not change).
73|
74|Per host, idle runners first; drain busy runners, then migrate:
75|
76|```
77|# 1. Pre-check (read-only, safe any time):
78|KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT=$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install \
79|  /path/to/runner/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service
80|
81|# 2. Rehearse:
82|scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id> --dry-run
83|
84|# 3. Migrate (snapshots unit + env, reloads, restarts, re-verifies):
85|scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id>
86|```
87|
88|The script refuses to overwrite an existing `current` link and prints
89|revert commands (copy the `.bak-<timestamp>` files back, reload,
90|restart). New installs need no migration: both installers
91|(`scripts/install-local-runner.sh`, `startRunner.sh`) already write
92|wrapper-based units. Verify after: `doctor` reports `status: ok` with
93|`entrypoint: wrapper`, and the next heartbeat shows the same version
94|as before.
95|
96|## Restart vs Update (Settings › Runners)
97|
98|Two separate actions, never combined:
99|
100|- **Restart** reboots the runner on its **current version** — no update
101|  check runs. It is destructive: any work running on that runner is
102|  stopped at once (the claim lease expires so the work re-queues, like a
103|  crash). The confirm window names the runner and warns about running
104|  work; use it when a runner looks stuck, not to change versions.
105|  Mechanism: the daemon writes a `restart-requested` sentinel beside the
106|  install root and exits 0; the wrapper consumes it and boots the SAME
107|  tree again. Restart therefore needs the wrapper entrypoint — a runner
108|  started as bare `node main.js` exits without rebooting (migrate to the
109|  wrapper, above).
110|- **Update** reinstalls the runner onto its **target version** — the
111|  exact pin when the runner is pinned, otherwise the newest compatible
112|  release — and applies only when the runner is idle (never interrupts
113|  work). A busy runner queues the update for the next idle point.
114|
115|## Per-runner version setting
116|
117|Each runner is set to **Latest** (default) or one exact release, via
118|the version dropdown on its Settings › Runners detail panel:
119|
120|- **Latest** tracks the newest release. It auto-updates at the next
121|  idle point (including right after a restart, once idle), and the
122|  backend nudges trailing runners at most daily. A red banner appears
123|  whenever a newer version exists than the one running — update (or
124|  wait for idle) to converge it.
125|- **Pinned** stays on exactly that release. Pinned runners never
126|  auto-update (no nudges, no idle installs, no restart-time installs);
127|  only the manual **Update** button installs the pin, and only when the
128|  pin is newer than the running version — the channel never downgrades,
129|  so a pin older than running shows a softer warning and the Update
130|  button stays disabled with the reason. Pick Latest or a newer pin to
131|  move forward.
132|
133|The dropdown lists Latest plus every fleet-known release (newest
134|first): each runner's running version plus the fleet recommended and
135|minimum knobs — offline-safe, no release catalogue fetch.
136|
137|## Triage: a runner says out of date
138|
139|Start on the runner host (or ask the host owner to run it) — the
140|doctor is read-only and never writes:
141|
142|```
143|$KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service
144|```
145|
146|Match the Settings › Runners badge to a cause:
147|
148|- **"update available" that never clears.** The runner trails
149|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (Latest runners) or its pin.
150|  If the doctor says `entrypoint: direct`, migrate to the wrapper
151|  (above) — staged updates can never boot there. If the env shows
152|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` (or `(unset)` with a host-level
153|  opt-out), the runner acked the nudge with "skipped: auto-update is
154|  disabled" — flip that switch. If the runner is pinned, only the
155|  manual Update button installs (pins never auto-update); a pin older
156|  than running refuses with "never downgrades" — pick Latest or a
157|  newer pin. If the recommended knob sits above every published
158|  release, lower it to the newest release. Otherwise the runner is
159|  likely just busy: it converges at the next idle check, or press
160|  Update now (idle-only, never interrupts work). Restart does NOT
161|  clear this — Restart reboots the same version.
162|- **"restart queued" that never clears / restart loop.** The runner
163|  collects `requestRestart` on every heartbeat but never reboots:
164|  check the journal for the `Runner restarting` line. If the line is
165|  there but no reboot follows, the runner is not supervised by the
166|  wrapper (bare `node main.js` exits instead of rebooting — migrate to
167|  the wrapper, above) or the install root is unwritable (look for
168|  `sentinel not written`). A `restart-requested` file left behind by a
169|  crash causes at most one extra boot on the next clean exit — the
170|  wrapper consumes it, never loops. Old runners that predate the
171|  command show a disabled Restart with "too old" guidance instead —
172|  update them manually.
173|- **"below minimum" / 409 loop.** The runner is under
174|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` and dispatch refuses it. It
175|  self-updates immediately when idle (interval bypassed). If it
176|  spins, check the journal for `Runner update` lines and treat the
177|  reason like an "update failed" below.
178|- **"update failed".** The next heartbeat carries `updateStatus`
179|  (`state: failed`, `reason`, `at`) — the badge tooltip shows it.
180|  Map the reason prefix: signature/key failure (release not signed
181|  by the pinned key — never hand-edit
182|  `PINNED_RELEASE_PUBLIC_KEY` in `runner/updates/verify.js` for a
183|  cut release); sha mismatch (re-download on next check); no asset
184|  for this platform (release is missing this host's tarball);
185|  incompatible with this backend (no newer release admits this
186|  backend's API — expected while the backend lags the release
187|  line); update lock held (a previous updater is still running or
188|  crashed mid-apply — stale locks self-heal); opted out (see
189|  above). Any failure keeps the old version running; fix the cause
190|  and the next idle check retries.
191|- **"rolled back" in the doctor.** Three crashed boots flipped
192|  `current` back to `previous`. Do not retry blindly: read the
193|  journal for the crash, fix forward with a patch release, and run
194|  the rollback drill above if the release is bad fleet-wide.
195|
196|Backend-side checks: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` and
197|`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` values, the fleet matrix row
198|for the runner (`runnerVersion`, `updateAvailable`, `belowMinimum`,
199|`updateStatus`), and whether a `requestUpdate` command is pending or
200|was acked within the last 24h (the auto-nudge cooldown).

1|#!/usr/bin/env bash
2|# lib.sh — shared helpers for the S5 ops scripts in this folder (bin/).
3|# Sourced, never executed directly. Shared because every script here needs
4|# the same three things: loud logging, loud death, and a validated HTTP GET.
5|#
6|# Rule for this task folder: an ops evidence script must never silently
7|# degrade. Every helper below either succeeds completely or reports a clear
8|# error and returns non-zero, so a baseline built from these scripts is
9|# trustworthy.
10|
11|# log <message...> — timestamped progress line on stderr. stdout stays clean
12|# because the scripts print evidence tables (jsonl/tsv) on stdout.
13|log() {
14|  printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" >&2
15|}
16|
17|# die <message...> — report a clear, fatal setup/usage error and exit 1.
18|# Used where there is nothing to salvage (missing tool, unreachable API,
19|# bad arguments). Runtime per-item failures are handled by the callers
20|# (recorded, counted, non-zero exit at the end) — see fleet-recount.sh.
21|die() {
22|  log "FATAL: $*"
23|  exit 1
24|}
25|
26|# require_commands <cmd...> — fail before touching anything if a tool is
27|# missing, so the failure is about the environment, not about half-written
28|# evidence files.
29|require_commands() {
30|  local missing=() cmd
31|  for cmd in "$@"; do
32|    command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$cmd")
33|  done
34|  if [ "${#missing[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
35|    die "missing required commands: ${missing[*]} — install them or run on the runner host"
36|  fi
37|}
38|
39|# write_atomic <dest> <src-file> — copy src-file next to dest and rename over
40|# it, so a crashed run never leaves a half-written evidence file that looks
41|# complete. Same directory => the final mv is an atomic rename.
42|write_atomic() {
43|  local dest="$1" src="$2" tmp="$dest.tmp.$$"
44|  if ! cp "$src" "$tmp"; then
45|    rm -f "$tmp"
46|    log "ERROR: cannot write $dest"
47|    return 1
48|  fi
49|  mv "$tmp" "$dest"
50|}
51|
52|# api_get_json <url> <dest> — GET url into dest as validated JSON.
53|#   - retries transient network failures (curl --retry-connrefused)
54|#   - fails on any HTTP error status (curl -f, so a 500/404 body is NOT kept)
55|#   - refuses to store a 200 body that is not valid JSON (an HTML error page
56|#     must never end up in the evidence store)
57|#   - writes dest atomically
58|# Returns non-zero with a clear stderr line on any failure.
59|api_get_json() {
60|  local url="$1" dest="$2" tmp
61|  tmp="$(mktemp)"
62|  if ! curl -sfS -m 60 --retry 3 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 2 -o "$tmp" "$url"; then
63|    rm -f "$tmp"
64|    log "ERROR: GET $url failed (HTTP error or host unreachable after retries)"
65|    return 1
66|  fi
67|  if ! jq -e 'type == "object" or type == "array"' "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
68|    rm -f "$tmp"
69|    log "ERROR: GET $url returned a body that is not valid JSON — refusing to store it in $dest"
70|    return 1
71|  fi
72|  write_atomic "$dest" "$tmp"
73|  rm -f "$tmp"
74|}
75|
76|# validate_task_prefix <prefix...> — task ids/prefixes get interpolated into
77|# shell commands (locally and over ssh) by e5-sweep.sh, so they must be hex
78|# and dashes only. Accepts a short prefix (8 hex chars) or a full UUID.
79|# This is the injection guard for the sweep: anything else is rejected before
80|# any command runs.
81|validate_task_prefix() {
82|  local p
83|  for p in "$@"; do
84|    if ! [[ "$p" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}(-[0-9a-fA-F]{4,12})*$ ]]; then
85|      die "bad task id prefix '$p' — expected 8 hex chars plus optional -hex groups (e.g. 7f6220c3 or the full UUID)"
86|    fi
87|  done
88|}

1|#!/usr/bin/env bash
2|# runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — record the fleet matrix
3|# (GET /runners + GET /deploy/status) and a per-runner convergence verdict.
4|# READ-ONLY against the backend; safe to run any time, any number of times.
5|#
6|# Outputs in <outdir>:
7|#   runners-<stamp>.json        raw GET /runners payload (evidence)
8|#   runners-<stamp>.tsv         flat fleet table incl. build sha/builtAt
9|#   deploy-status-<stamp>.json  raw GET /deploy/status payload
10|#   verdict-<stamp>.txt         one line per named runner: CONVERGED or the reasons why not
11|#
12|# Convergence rule (S5 success criterion 1): runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND the
13|# running build's reported git sha contains the fix commit — verified locally
14|# with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fixCommit> <buildSha>`, because a version
15|# string alone cannot prove which code is running. If the runner reports no
16|# build sha, the verdict says so instead of guessing.
17|#
18|# Knobs (env):
19|#   KAINBAIN_API_BASE            default http://192.168.1.206:3100
20|#   KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS    default "local-alpha,server2-alpha"
21|#   KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT       default 046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4 (the 046a6391 deterministic-git-failure change)
22|#
23|# Exit codes: 0 snapshot written (converged or not — read verdict-<stamp>.txt);
24|#   1 setup or API failure (nothing trustworthy written);
25|#   3 snapshot written, --require-converged given, but not all named runners converged.
26|set -euo pipefail
27|SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
28|# shellcheck source=lib.sh
29|source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"
30|
31|# fix_in_build <buildSha|""|null> — prints true/false/null. null = cannot tell
32|# (no sha reported, or sha unknown to the local repo). Uses the local Kainbain
33|# checkout as the commit database — read-only git queries only.
34|fix_in_build() {
35|  local sha="$1" repo_root="$2" fix_commit="$3"
36|  if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ "$sha" = "null" ]; then
37|    echo null
38|    return 0
39|  fi
40|  if ! git -C "$repo_root" cat-file -e "$sha^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
41|    echo null
42|    return 0
43|  fi
44|  if git -C "$repo_root" merge-base --is-ancestor "$fix_commit" "$sha" 2>/dev/null; then
45|    echo true
46|  else
47|    echo false
48|  fi
49|}
50|
51|# verdict_for <runners.json> <runnerId> — prints the verdict JSON object for one
52|# runner (jq/runner-verdict.jq + the git ancestry check).
53|verdict_for() {
54|  local runners_json="$1" runner_id="$2" repo_root="$3" fix_commit="$4"
55|  local runner sha fix
56|  runner="$(jq -c --arg id "$runner_id" '.[] | select(.runnerId == $id) // empty' "$runners_json")"
57|  if [ -z "$runner" ]; then
58|    printf '{"runnerId":"%s","converged":false,"reasons":["runner not present in GET /runners (offline/revoked?)"]}\n' "$runner_id"
59|    return 0
60|  fi
61|  sha="$(printf '%s' "$runner" | jq -r '.facts.versions.build.sha // ""')"
62|  fix="$(fix_in_build "$sha" "$repo_root" "$fix_commit")"
63|  jq -n -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/runner-verdict.jq" --argjson runner "$runner" --argjson fixInBuild "$fix"
64|}
65|
66|main() {
67|  require_commands curl jq git date mktemp
68|  local outdir="${1:-}"
69|  [ -n "$outdir" ] || die "usage: runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged]"
70|  local require_converged=0
71|  if [ "${2:-}" = "--require-converged" ]; then require_converged=1; fi
72|
73|  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
74|  local named="${KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS:-local-alpha,server2-alpha}"
75|  local fix_commit="${KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT:-046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4}"
76|  local task_dir repo_root stamp
77|  task_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
78|  repo_root="$(git -C "$task_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
79|  stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
80|  mkdir -p "$outdir"
81|
82|  log "runners-snapshot api=$api_base outdir=$outdir named=$named fix=$fix_commit"
83|
84|  local runners_json="$outdir/runners-$stamp.json" deploy_json="$outdir/deploy-status-$stamp.json"
85|  api_get_json "$api_base/runners" "$runners_json" \
86|    || die "GET $api_base/runners failed — nothing written to $outdir"
87|  api_get_json "$api_base/deploy/status" "$deploy_json" \
88|    || { log "WARN: GET /deploy/status failed — continuing with /runners only"; rm -f "$deploy_json"; }
89|
90|  jq -r -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/runners-tsv.jq" "$runners_json" > "$outdir/runners-$stamp.tsv"
91|
92|  local verdict_json="$outdir/verdict-$stamp.json" verdict_txt="$outdir/verdict-$stamp.txt"
93|  : > "$verdict_json.tmp"
94|  local IFS=',' r all_converged=1 v
95|  for r in $named; do
96|    v="$(verdict_for "$runners_json" "$r" "$repo_root" "$fix_commit")"
97|    printf '%s\n' "$v" >> "$verdict_json.tmp"
98|    if printf '%s' "$v" | jq -e '.converged == true' >/dev/null; then
99|      printf 'CONVERGED    %s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$v" | jq -r '[.runnerId, .runnerVersion, (.buildSha // "no-sha")] | join(" ")')" >> "$verdict_txt"
100|    else
101|      all_converged=0
102|      printf 'NOT-CONVERGED %s — %s\n' "$r" "$(printf '%s' "$v" | jq -r '.reasons | join("; ")')" >> "$verdict_txt"
103|    fi
104|  done
105|  jq -s '.' "$verdict_json.tmp" > "$verdict_json" && rm -f "$verdict_json.tmp"
106|
107|  {
108|    echo "# runner convergence verdict — $(date -u +%FT%TZ) — fix commit $fix_commit"
109|    echo "# converged = runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND running build sha contains the fix commit"
110|    cat "$verdict_txt"
111|  } > "$verdict_txt.hdr" && mv "$verdict_txt.hdr" "$verdict_txt"
112|
113|  echo "wrote $outdir/runners-$stamp.{json,tsv} ${deploy_json:+deploy-status-$stamp.json} verdict-$stamp.{json,txt}"
114|  cat "$outdir/runners-$stamp.tsv"
115|  echo "--- verdict:"
116|  cat "$verdict_txt"
117|
118|  if [ "$require_converged" = 1 ] && [ "$all_converged" = 0 ]; then
119|    log "--require-converged: not all named runners converged (see $verdict_txt)"
120|    exit 3
121|  fi
122|}
123|
124|if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
125|  main "$@"
126|fi

## S5 — Roll out 0.2.x runners and run the fleet before/after recount (ops + verification)

**Covers Cause 5 verification and unlocks diagnosis of Causes 3–4.** Deployed runners
are 0.1.0 (main `f430f53`, 11-11); repo is 0.2.0 with interrupt reasons and
deterministic-git-failure handling (`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in `7ac148ce`).
Rollout is backend-nudged, at most daily per runner, idle-converge
(`docs/runner-update-runbook.md`), so lag is expected — but until it lands, every new
interrupt is still bare and every commit-hook rejection still crash-loops.

**Proposed steps:**
1. Confirm both runners (`local-alpha`, `server2-alpha`) converge to the build
   containing `046a6391` per the runbook; record `GET /runners` versions before/after.
2. Re-run the `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2` counts + GUIDE-07 §5 fleet script: bare
   interrupts should drop to ~0, reasons should name Causes 1/3/4 directly, and
   deterministic commit failures should surface as FAILED completions with
   `gitFailure` payloads, never as interrupts.
3. Run the E5 forensics sweep (GUIDE-05 §4): for each remaining post-`finished`
   interrupt, check `kb-<taskId>` worktrees (`158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`,
   `7f6220c3`) for stage-output-commit presence (present → Cause 2/4 territory;
   absent → Cause 5). Only if E5 finds commit-loop cases the `046a6391` fix does not
   cover should a new Cause-5 code task be created.
4. Record the post-rollout counts in the task folder as the new baseline for S1–S4.

**How to confirm the underlying bugs:** this task *is* the confirmation harness —
before/after counts plus the journal sweeps (E3 `Backend 413`, E4 502/fetch-fail,
E5 hook/commit lines). No new unit tests; deliverable is the recount + version record.
**Parallel/blocking:** runs in parallel with all code work; only prod *confirmation*
of S3/S4/S2-runner-half waits on it.
**Risk:** low. Follow the runbook; do not force-restart runners mid-assignment to
speed convergence (observe only — forced restarts are PROD-ACTION and risk new
interrupts, which is exactly what we are measuring).

## S6 — Fix the misleading display: resume label + "Tried N times" (backend + frontend)

**Answers the amplifier's display half — the cheapest, lowest-risk task, and the one
that fixes what the reporter actually saw.** `autoResumeTask` uses one history string
for both recovery routes, so 100 runner-path resumes display as "server restarts that
never happened" (0 recorded); `summarizeStageRuns` counts every `Resumed` row into
`tryCount`, producing the screenshot's ×6/×10/×11 badges.

**Proposed change:**
1. Backend (`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js`): distinct history strings per
   recovery route — keep `Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue`
   for genuine reconcile recoveries, add e.g. `Auto-resumed after runner interrupt —
   prioritised in queue` (include runner id + reason when present) for runner-path
   resumes. Use the existing `interruptedBy` marker to pick the route.
2. Frontend (`frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js` `summarizeStageRuns`,
   `:483-536`): exclude `Resumed` rows from `tryCount` (they are infra re-tries, not
   stage attempts) — or show them separately (e.g. `Tried 2 times · 4 infra resumes`).
   Update `formatTryCount` (`:556`) accordingly.
3. Update the existing pins that encode current behaviour (`taskFormatters.test.js`
   `summarizeStageRuns` cases, `taskScheduler.test.js:896` autoResume block,
   `stallRecovery`/`startupRecovery` integration tests referencing the label) —
   this is an intended contract change, not a regression; each updated assertion must
   state the new expected string/count explicitly.

**Tests:** `api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeLabel.test.js` (GUIDE-07 §2 — pin-then-red),
frontend `summarizeStageRuns` pin-then-red (§4). Full gate: `npm run test:api`,
`npm run test:frontend`.
**How to confirm the bug:** local — the §2/§4 pin tests pass on current code, proving
the mislabel and the inflation; the red tests fail until fixed. Prod (read-only):

# Runner update runbook

Operator procedures for the runner self-update channel (Option A,
`docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md`): cutting releases,
rolling back, migrating hosts to the wrapper, and triaging a runner
that says out of date. The backend directs version selection but never
serves runner bytes (R05) — every procedure below preserves that.

## Cutting a runner release (normal path)

The tag is the version source of truth; the pipeline cuts it.

1. Bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json` (plain semver for
   fleet releases, e.g. `0.2.0`; suffixed tags like `0.3.0-rc.1` for
   canaries — v1 runners skip pre-releases automatically).
2. If the release needs a newer backend API, update the
   `requires.backendApi` range in the same file (e.g.
   `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`). The release builder refuses manifests without a
   compat claim, and runners filter on this range.
3. Merge to the main line through the normal review flow.
4. Publish the runner (`publish.sh` with the runner component). The
   publish cuts and pushes the annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which
   triggers `runner-release.yml`: full update-channel test gate, four
   platform archives, signed `manifest.json` + `.minisig`, GitHub
   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).
5. Raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the new version on
   the backend. That is the one managed place: trailers light the
   "update available" badge and the backend auto-nudges command-capable
   ones (`requestUpdate`, at most daily per runner). Runners converge
   on idle with no SSH. Leave `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` alone
   unless this is a breaking release (the 409 floor stops dispatch).

## Cutting a runner release (emergency path)

When the pipeline cannot cut the tag (CI down, urgent patch), tag by
hand from the release commit — the same builder runs:

```
git tag -a runner-vX.Y.Z -m "Runner runner-vX.Y.Z" <full-sha>
git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z
```

Then follow step 5 above. Never move an existing tag: cut a patch
version forward instead.

## Rollback drill (bad release, no host access needed)

1. Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release so `releases/latest`
   resolves to the prior tag.
2. Lower `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (and
   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` if it was raised past the bad
   version) to stop badge nagging and 409 loops.
3. Cut a patch release forward (normal path above). The updater never
   downgrades: runners still on older versions pick the prior release
   up on their next idle check, while runners already on the bad
   release stay there until the patch supersedes it.
4. Two automatic outs: a release that crashes on boot rolls itself
   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
   is cut.

Drill timing to record: un-publish → badges clear, patch cut →
fleet converged.

## Migrating a host to the wrapper

Direct `node main.js` units re-exec the same old directory on every
restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at
the stable wrapper shim — onto the SAME version (no update is staged,
so the fleet version does not change).

Per host, idle runners first; drain busy runners, then migrate:

```
# 1. Pre-check (read-only, safe any time):
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT=$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install \
  /path/to/runner/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service

# Runner update runbook

Operator procedures for the runner self-update channel (Option A,
`docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md`): cutting releases,
rolling back, migrating hosts to the wrapper, and triaging a runner
that says out of date. The backend directs version selection but never
serves runner bytes (R05) — every procedure below preserves that.

## Cutting a runner release (normal path)

The tag is the version source of truth; the pipeline cuts it.

1. Bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json` (plain semver for
   fleet releases, e.g. `0.2.0`; suffixed tags like `0.3.0-rc.1` for
   canaries — v1 runners skip pre-releases automatically).
2. If the release needs a newer backend API, update the
   `requires.backendApi` range in the same file (e.g.
   `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`). The release builder refuses manifests without a
   compat claim, and runners filter on this range.
3. Merge to the main line through the normal review flow.
4. Publish the runner (`publish.sh` with the runner component). The
   publish cuts and pushes the annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which
   triggers `runner-release.yml`: full update-channel test gate, four
   platform archives, signed `manifest.json` + `.minisig`, GitHub
   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).
5. Raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the new version on
   the backend. That is the one managed place: trailers light the
   "update available" badge and the backend auto-nudges command-capable
   ones (`requestUpdate`, at most daily per runner). Runners converge
   on idle with no SSH. Leave `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` alone
   unless this is a breaking release (the 409 floor stops dispatch).

## Cutting a runner release (emergency path)

When the pipeline cannot cut the tag (CI down, urgent patch), tag by
hand from the release commit — the same builder runs:

```
git tag -a runner-vX.Y.Z -m "Runner runner-vX.Y.Z" <full-sha>
git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z
```

Then follow step 5 above. Never move an existing tag: cut a patch
version forward instead.

## Rollback drill (bad release, no host access needed)

1. Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release so `releases/latest`
   resolves to the prior tag.
2. Lower `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (and
   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` if it was raised past the bad
   version) to stop badge nagging and 409 loops.
3. Cut a patch release forward (normal path above). The updater never
   downgrades: runners still on older versions pick the prior release
   up on their next idle check, while runners already on the bad
   release stay there until the patch supersedes it.
4. Two automatic outs: a release that crashes on boot rolls itself
   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
   is cut.

Drill timing to record: un-publish → badges clear, patch cut →
fleet converged.

## Migrating a host to the wrapper

Direct `node main.js` units re-exec the same old directory on every
restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at
the stable wrapper shim — onto the SAME version (no update is staged,
so the fleet version does not change).

Per host, idle runners first; drain busy runners, then migrate:

```

KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT=$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install \
  /path/to/runner/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service

## Approach — make observation easy, then observe

This task changes nothing; its failure mode is fuzzy, non-reproducible numbers.
So Phase 0 ("make change easy") builds all reusable observation tooling first —
frozen scripts, record templates, access checks, and the BEFORE snapshot — and
only then do the time-ordered phases run. Big/volatile evidence comes early:
the BEFORE recount and the E5 sweep run before the convergence wait, because
interrupts keep accruing and worktree exhibits keep getting reaped (all four
E5 seed exhibits are already absent from this host). The long pole — idle
convergence at most daily per runner — waits in Phase 3 without blocking
Phase 1/2 evidence.

Attribution boundaries (what S5 may and may not claim): S1 (cap counting),
S2-backend (413 limit), S4 (transient tolerance), S6 (labels/counts) all change
the same signals. S5's after-recount MUST record the backend build number
(`GET /deploy/status`) and which sibling fixes have landed, and split new
interrupts by timestamp against each runner's converge time. Only interrupts
timestamped after a runner converged to 0.2.x count as "after" for S5.
`escalated` dropping is an S1 signal, not an S5 gate; the S5 gates are bare→~0,
reasons present, and FAILED+`gitFailure` instead of commit-loop interrupts.

## Phase 2 — E5 forensics sweep (early: exhibits are volatile)

`1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`, plus any new ones from 1.1):

2.1 Worktree check per host (read-only, never reap): resolve the runner work
    root on that host first, then
    `git -C $WORK_ROOT/kb-<taskId>* log --oneline -3` and look for a
    stage-output commit matching the execution window. Present → Cause 2/4
    territory; absent → Cause 5 suspect. Record exact SHAs or exact absence.
2.2 Journal join (same host, same window): `Runner failed:` line text +
    restart-counter deltas — names hook/commit vs 413 vs 502/fetch-fail.
2.3 Fallback chain when a worktree is absent (already the case on server2-alpha
    for all four seeds): (a) check the sibling host; (b) check `origin` for the
    stage-output SHA (pushed = commit succeeded, Cause 2/4); (c) journal line
    alone; (d) if all absent, record an explicit evidence gap — never guess.
2.4 Verdict per interrupt: Cause-2/4 vs Cause-5-covered-by-`046a6391` vs
    Cause-5-NOT-covered. The third verdict is the ONLY trigger for new code:
    if and only if E5 finds commit-loop cases `046a6391` does not cover
    (a deterministic failure class outside `HOOK_REJECTED`/`COMMIT_FAILED`/
    `MERGE_CONFLICT` that still crash-loops on 0.2.x), file a NEW Cause-5

    the runbook ("a runner says out of date") — `entrypoint: direct` vs
    wrapper, `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` opt-out, pinned version, pin
    older than running, recommended knob above every release, `updateStatus`
    failure reason — and record the blocking cause. Fixes (migrate, flip the
    switch, Update button) are PROD-ACTION: propose, do not perform.
3.4 NEVER to speed convergence: force-restart mid-assignment, Update-on-busy,
    reaping worktrees, re-running parked tasks. Any of these manufactures the
    interrupts being measured (q9 / PROD-ACTION ban).

named blocking cause. Under the q3-fallback (before-now/stop), Phase 3 becomes
a scheduled follow-up run instead of a same-run wait.

## Phase 4 — AFTER recount + journal sweeps (after both converge)

4.1 AFTER snapshot: raw `GET /runners` JSON + fleet script → `RECOUNT-AFTER.md`
    (§2 table + per-task rows), timestamped ≥ both converge times.
4.2 Split new interrupts at each runner's converge time; evaluate the S5 gates
    on post-converge interrupts only: bare → ~0; reasons name Causes 1/3/4
    (cap strings, setup-fault messages, transient 502/fetch-fail strings);
    deterministic commit failures arrive as FAILED completions carrying
    `gitFailure` payloads (`kind`/`phase`/`summary`) with NO interrupt row.

    (expect none-new after S2 lands; any 413 on 0.2.x must pair with a FAILED
    completion, never a crash loop), E4 502/`fetch failed` crash lines
    (expect crash-restarts to persist until S4 lands — reasons now name them),
    hook/commit lines (expect single `commit failed (...)` + FAILED, no
    restart storm).

    have deployed, and any deploys that restarted the backend in-window

So Phase 0 ("make change easy") builds all reusable observation tooling first —
frozen scripts, record templates, access checks, and the BEFORE snapshot — and
only then do the time-ordered phases run. Big/volatile evidence comes early:
the BEFORE recount and the E5 sweep run before the convergence wait, because
interrupts keep accruing and worktree exhibits keep getting reaped (all four

convergence at most daily per runner — waits in Phase 3 without blocking
Phase 1/2 evidence.

## Validation & assurance plan (how we know it worked)

No unit tests by design (ops task — RESPONSE.md S5: "No new unit tests;
deliverable is the recount + version record"). Assurance instead comes from
executed procedures with saved evidence, each claim cross-checked two ways:

| Claim | Primary evidence | Independent cross-check |
|---|---|---|
| Runners on fix build | `GET /runners` version facts | `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0` + heartbeat build fields |
| Bare → ~0 | Fleet script `bare` count post-converge | Reason-vocabulary audit (1.3): every new interrupt carries a reason naming a cause |
| No commit crash-loops | FAILED + `gitFailure` completions, no interrupt row | Journal: single `commit failed` per incident, no restart storm |
| E5 classification | Worktree stage-output-commit presence | Journal `Runner failed:` line + origin SHA check |
| No server-restart orphans | `server_restart` count stays 0 | Backend build/`engine.updatedAt` divergence log (Cause-6 upkeep) |

Per-phase gates above double as the test plan: a phase is done only when its
artifact file exists with the named content. Negative controls: (a) BEFORE
snapshot must show still-bare new interrupts (proves the premise that 0.1.0
emits no reasons); (b) any reasoned non-cap interrupt pre-converge, or any
bare interrupt post-converge, fails its gate and must be explained, not
averaged away. Docs assurance: every record file carries timestamps, raw
command output (or the raw JSON), and the exact re-run command.

This task changes nothing; its failure mode is fuzzy, non-reproducible numbers.
So Phase 0 ("make change easy") builds all reusable observation tooling first —
frozen scripts, record templates, access checks, and the BEFORE snapshot — and
only then do the time-ordered phases run. Big/volatile evidence comes early:
the BEFORE recount and the E5 sweep run before the convergence wait, because
interrupts keep accruing and worktree exhibits keep getting reaped (all four
E5 seed exhibits are already absent from this host). The long pole — idle
convergence at most daily per runner — waits in Phase 3 without blocking
Phase 1/2 evidence.

S2-backend (413 limit), S4 (transient tolerance), S6 (labels/counts) all change

## Validation & assurance plan (how we know it worked)

No unit tests by design (ops task — RESPONSE.md S5: "No new unit tests;
deliverable is the recount + version record"). Assurance instead comes from
executed procedures with saved evidence, each claim cross-checked two ways:

| Claim | Primary evidence | Independent cross-check |
|---|---|---|
| Runners on fix build | `GET /runners` version facts | `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0` + heartbeat build fields |
| Bare → ~0 | Fleet script `bare` count post-converge | Reason-vocabulary audit (1.3): every new interrupt carries a reason naming a cause |
| No commit crash-loops | FAILED + `gitFailure` completions, no interrupt row | Journal: single `commit failed` per incident, no restart storm |
| E5 classification | Worktree stage-output-commit presence | Journal `Runner failed:` line + origin SHA check |
| No server-restart orphans | `server_restart` count stays 0 | Backend build/`engine.updatedAt` divergence log (Cause-6 upkeep) |

Per-phase gates above double as the test plan: a phase is done only when its
artifact file exists with the named content. Negative controls: (a) BEFORE
snapshot must show still-bare new interrupts (proves the premise that 0.1.0
emits no reasons); (b) any reasoned non-cap interrupt pre-converge, or any
bare interrupt post-converge, fails its gate and must be explained, not
averaged away. Docs assurance: every record file carries timestamps, raw
command output (or the raw JSON), and the exact re-run command.

## Approach — make observation easy, then observe

This task changes nothing; its failure mode is fuzzy, non-reproducible numbers.
So Phase 0 ("make change easy") builds all reusable observation tooling first —
frozen scripts, record templates, access checks, and the BEFORE snapshot — and
only then do the time-ordered phases run. Big/volatile evidence comes early:
the BEFORE recount and the E5 sweep run before the convergence wait, because
interrupts keep accruing and worktree exhibits keep getting reaped (all four
E5 seed exhibits are already absent from this host). The long pole — idle
convergence at most daily per runner — waits in Phase 3 without blocking
Phase 1/2 evidence.

Attribution boundaries (what S5 may and may not claim): S1 (cap counting),
S2-backend (413 limit), S4 (transient tolerance), S6 (labels/counts) all change
the same signals. S5's after-recount MUST record the backend build number
(`GET /deploy/status`) and which sibling fixes have landed, and split new
interrupts by timestamp against each runner's converge time. Only interrupts
timestamped after a runner converged to 0.2.x count as "after" for S5.
`escalated` dropping is an S1 signal, not an S5 gate; the S5 gates are bare→~0,
reasons present, and FAILED+`gitFailure` instead of commit-loop interrupts.

`1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`, plus any new ones from 1.1):

## Validation & assurance plan (how we know it worked)

No unit tests by design (ops task — RESPONSE.md S5: "No new unit tests;
deliverable is the recount + version record"). Assurance instead comes from
executed procedures with saved evidence, each claim cross-checked two ways:

| Claim | Primary evidence | Independent cross-check |
|---|---|---|
| Runners on fix build | `GET /runners` version facts | `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0` + heartbeat build fields |
| Bare → ~0 | Fleet script `bare` count post-converge | Reason-vocabulary audit (1.3): every new interrupt carries a reason naming a cause |
| No commit crash-loops | FAILED + `gitFailure` completions, no interrupt row | Journal: single `commit failed` per incident, no restart storm |
| E5 classification | Worktree stage-output-commit presence | Journal `Runner failed:` line + origin SHA check |
| No server-restart orphans | `server_restart` count stays 0 | Backend build/`engine.updatedAt` divergence log (Cause-6 upkeep) |

Per-phase gates above double as the test plan: a phase is done only when its
artifact file exists with the named content. Negative controls: (a) BEFORE
snapshot must show still-bare new interrupts (proves the premise that 0.1.0
emits no reasons); (b) any reasoned non-cap interrupt pre-converge, or any
bare interrupt post-converge, fails its gate and must be explained, not
averaged away. Docs assurance: every record file carries timestamps, raw
command output (or the raw JSON), and the exact re-run command.

1|#!/usr/bin/env bash
2|# runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — record the fleet matrix
3|# (GET /runners + GET /deploy/status) and a per-runner convergence verdict.
4|# READ-ONLY against the backend; safe to run any time, any number of times.
5|#
6|# Outputs in <outdir>:
7|#   runners-<stamp>.json        raw GET /runners payload (evidence)
8|#   runners-<stamp>.tsv         flat fleet table incl. build sha/builtAt
9|#   deploy-status-<stamp>.json  raw GET /deploy/status payload
10|#   verdict-<stamp>.txt         one line per named runner: CONVERGED or the reasons why not
11|#
12|# Convergence rule (S5 success criterion 1): runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND the
13|# running build's reported git sha contains the fix commit — verified locally
14|# with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fixCommit> <buildSha>`, because a version
15|# string alone cannot prove which code is running. If the runner reports no
16|# build sha, the verdict says so instead of guessing.
17|#
18|# Knobs (env):
19|#   KAINBAIN_API_BASE            default http://192.168.1.206:3100
20|#   KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS    default "local-alpha,server2-alpha"
21|#   KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT       default 046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4 (the 046a6391 deterministic-git-failure change)
22|#
23|# Exit codes: 0 snapshot written (converged or not — read verdict-<stamp>.txt);
24|#   1 setup or API failure (nothing trustworthy written);
25|#   3 snapshot written, --require-converged given, but not all named runners converged.
26|set -euo pipefail
27|SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
28|# shellcheck source=lib.sh
29|source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"
30|
31|# fix_in_build <buildSha|""|null> — prints true/false/null. null = cannot tell
32|# (no sha reported, or sha unknown to the local repo). Uses the local Kainbain
33|# checkout as the commit database — read-only git queries only.
34|fix_in_build() {
35|  local sha="$1" repo_root="$2" fix_commit="$3"
36|  if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ "$sha" = "null" ]; then
37|    echo null
38|    return 0
39|  fi
40|  if ! git -C "$repo_root" cat-file -e "$sha^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
41|    echo null
42|    return 0
43|  fi
44|  if git -C "$repo_root" merge-base --is-ancestor "$fix_commit" "$sha" 2>/dev/null; then
45|    echo true
46|  else
47|    echo false
48|  fi
49|}
50|
51|# verdict_for <runners.json> <runnerId> — prints the verdict JSON object for one
52|# runner (jq/runner-verdict.jq + the git ancestry check).
53|verdict_for() {
54|  local runners_json="$1" runner_id="$2" repo_root="$3" fix_commit="$4"
55|  local runner sha fix
56|  runner="$(jq -c --arg id "$runner_id" '.[] | select(.runnerId == $id) // empty' "$runners_json")"
57|  if [ -z "$runner" ]; then
58|    printf '{"runnerId":"%s","converged":false,"reasons":["runner not present in GET /runners (offline/revoked?)"]}\n' "$runner_id"
59|    return 0
60|  fi
61|  sha="$(printf '%s' "$runner" | jq -r '.facts.versions.build.sha // ""')"
62|  fix="$(fix_in_build "$sha" "$repo_root" "$fix_commit")"
63|  jq -n -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/runner-verdict.jq" --argjson runner "$runner" --argjson fixInBuild "$fix"
64|}
65|
66|main() {
67|  require_commands curl jq git date mktemp
68|  local outdir="${1:-}"
69|  [ -n "$outdir" ] || die "usage: runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged]"
70|  local require_converged=0
71|  if [ "${2:-}" = "--require-converged" ]; then require_converged=1; fi
72|
73|  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
74|  local named="${KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS:-local-alpha,server2-alpha}"
75|  local fix_commit="${KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT:-046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4}"
76|  local task_dir repo_root stamp
77|  task_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
78|  repo_root="$(git -C "$task_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
79|  stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
80|  mkdir -p "$outdir"
81|
82|  log "runners-snapshot api=$api_base outdir=$outdir named=$named fix=$fix_commit"
83|
84|  local runners_json="$outdir/runners-$stamp.json" deploy_json="$outdir/deploy-status-$stamp.json"
85|  api_get_json "$api_base/runners" "$runners_json" \
86|    || die "GET $api_base/runners failed — nothing written to $outdir"
87|  api_get_json "$api_base/deploy/status" "$deploy_json" \
88|    || { log "WARN: GET /deploy/status failed — continuing with /runners only"; rm -f "$deploy_json"; }
89|
90|  jq -r -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/runners-tsv.jq" "$runners_json" > "$outdir/runners-$stamp.tsv"
91|
92|  local verdict_json="$outdir/verdict-$stamp.json" verdict_txt="$outdir/verdict-$stamp.txt"
93|  : > "$verdict_json.tmp"
94|  local IFS=',' r all_converged=1 v
95|  for r in $named; do
96|    v="$(verdict_for "$runners_json" "$r" "$repo_root" "$fix_commit")"
97|    printf '%s\n' "$v" >> "$verdict_json.tmp"
98|    if printf '%s' "$v" | jq -e '.converged == true' >/dev/null; then
99|      printf 'CONVERGED    %s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$v" | jq -r '[.runnerId, .runnerVersion, (.buildSha // "no-sha")] | join(" ")')" >> "$verdict_txt"
100|    else
101|      all_converged=0
102|      printf 'NOT-CONVERGED %s — %s\n' "$r" "$(printf '%s' "$v" | jq -r '.reasons | join("; ")')" >> "$verdict_txt"
103|    fi
104|  done
105|  jq -s '.' "$verdict_json.tmp" > "$verdict_json" && rm -f "$verdict_json.tmp"
106|
107|  {
108|    echo "# runner convergence verdict — $(date -u +%FT%TZ) — fix commit $fix_commit"
109|    echo "# converged = runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND running build sha contains the fix commit"
110|    cat "$verdict_txt"
111|  } > "$verdict_txt.hdr" && mv "$verdict_txt.hdr" "$verdict_txt"
112|
113|  echo "wrote $outdir/runners-$stamp.{json,tsv} ${deploy_json:+deploy-status-$stamp.json} verdict-$stamp.{json,txt}"
114|  cat "$outdir/runners-$stamp.tsv"
115|  echo "--- verdict:"
116|  cat "$verdict_txt"
117|
118|  if [ "$require_converged" = 1 ] && [ "$all_converged" = 0 ]; then
119|    log "--require-converged: not all named runners converged (see $verdict_txt)"
120|    exit 3
121|  fi
122|}
123|
124|if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
125|  main "$@"
126|fi
